title: Little sentences

parent.learn: Sight words: I, a, the, is, can, see, my, go, to, and.
parent.why: These words come in almost every sentence and many can't be sounded out (like “the”), so they are learnt by sight.

parent.learn: A sentence starts with a capital letter and ends with a full stop.
parent.why: The capital says “start here” and the full stop says “this idea is finished” — so the reader knows where to pause.
Without spaces, “Icanrun” is hard to read; spaces show where one word ends and the next begins.
Adding -s tells the reader there is more than one — English often shows “many” this way.

ask: Read with me: “I can see a cat.”
Find the word “the” on this page. How many times is it there?
Say a sentence about your toy.
One dog, two…? One ball, three…?
Point to the full stop in this sentence.
Put these words in order: run / I / can.

rounds.t: “I can see a cat.” What can I see?
rounds.h: The last word tells us: a cat.
t-h-e: the. It is a sight word — learn it by its look.
i-s: is, as in “It is hot”.
c-a-n: can, as in “I can run”.
More than one: add s — cats.
More than one: add s — apples.
The full stop shows the idea is finished.
“I have a ball.” With “I” we say have.
The sun gives heat, so it is hot.
It starts with a capital, ends with a full stop, and makes sense.

rounds.t: “Ravi has a red bag.” What colour is the bag?
“Tom is in the bus.” Where is Tom?
Put the words in order: cat / The / sleeps
rounds.h: Who? The cat. Does what? Sleeps. The capital T shows “The” goes first.

rounds.t: How many words are in “I like mangoes.”?
rounds.h: Count the gaps: I / like / mangoes — 3 words.
